subtitle: The Mystic Whose Song Outlived the Chronicles

panels.shot: wide, misty valley vista with river and terraced fields, Lal Ded in the mid-ground walking along a path, mouth slightly open as if mid-verse
panels.action: Lal Ded walks barefoot along a Kashmiri village path at dusk, shawl wrapped loosely, peasants pause from their tasks as her unseen song seems to hang over snow-lined peaks and willow-lined streams.

dialogue.text: Courts forgot her, chronicles fell silent; yet for six centuries Kashmir has whispered Lal Ded’s name in every field and shrine.

i18n.hi: दरबार भूले, इतिहास चुप हुआ; पर छह सौ साल से हर खेत, हर दरगाह में कश्मीर धीरे से उसका नाम कहता रहा – लाल डेड.

panels.shot: high aerial over the Kashmir valley, sweeping from snowy Pir Panjal down to the Jhelum and clustered settlements
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view shows the broad Kashmir valley in the 14th century, snow ridges guarding a bowl of fields, rivers and small towns with wooden houses and temples amid orchards.

dialogue.text: In the fourteenth century, Kashmir was changing: old Shaiva temples, new sultans, caravans from distant lands, all meeting in this high valley of rivers and snow.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी का कश्मीर बदल रहा था: पुराने शैव मंदिर, नए सुल्तान, दूर देशों से कारवाँ – सब नदियों और बर्फ की इस ऊँची घाटी में मिलने लगे.

panels.shot: medium shot inside a modest Kashmiri home, warm interior light, focus on young Lal Ded at the doorway
panels.action: A young Lal Ded stands in a simple wooden house near Pandrethan, face half-lit by a smoky lamp, looking out toward distant temple spires and farmland as elders sit in the background.

dialogue.text: Later storytellers place her near Pandrethan, a girl called Lalla, hearing Sanskrit chants in shrines yet speaking Kashmiri in courtyard and field.

i18n.hi: किस्से उसे पनध्राथन के पास रखते हैं – लल्ला नाम की लड़की, देवालय में संस्कृत मंत्र सुनती, आँगन और खेतों में कश्मीरी बोलती.

panels.shot: close-up on Lal Ded’s face, eyes closed, lips parted as if repeating a verse, background faintly showing an old Shaiva temple
panels.action: Lal Ded as a young woman sits near a stone Shaiva shrine, eyes closed, fingers moving on prayer beads as temple bells ring softly behind her in the mist.

dialogue.text: Tradition remembers her drawn to Shaiva practice, to teachers of Kashmir’s mystic path, though the details are mist, not stone.

i18n.hi: रिवायत कहती है, वो शैव साधना की ओर खिंची, कश्मीर की रहस्यमयी राह के गुरुओं की ओर – पर बातें धुंध हैं, शिला नहीं.

panels.shot: wide riverside shot, Lal Ded walking alone along the Jhelum, distant town and wooden bridge in background
panels.action: Now older, Lal Ded walks along the riverbank near Bijbehara, bare feet on wet earth, her shawl plain, her posture free, fishermen and women at the water’s edge turning to watch.

dialogue.text: What is certain comes not from records but from memory: a woman wandering from village to village, refusing confinement, reciting her insight aloud.

i18n.hi: यक़ीन बस याद से आता है, लेख से नहीं: एक औरत गाँव–गाँव भटकती, बंधन ठुकराती, अपना बोध ऊँची आवाज़ में सुनाती.

panels.shot: medium shot of a village courtyard, children and elders gathered loosely, Lal Ded standing slightly elevated on a stone
panels.action: In a village courtyard, Lal Ded stands on a flat stone, eyes bright, hand raised lightly as farmers, potters and children encircle her, their faces intent as if catching each word.

dialogue.text: Her vakhs were short, sharp utterances, spoken in Kashmiri; villagers heard everyday speech suddenly carry the weight of scripture.

i18n.hi: उसके वख छोटे, तीखे बोल थे, खालिस कश्मीरी में; गाँववालों ने रोज़ की ज़बान में अचानक शास्त्रों का भार महसूस किया.

panels.shot: tight three-quarter close-up, Lal Ded’s mouth as if mid-verse, distant snow peaks blurred behind
panels.action: A close view shows Lal Ded mid-utterance, face weathered yet luminous, gaze turned inward, with the hazy outline of snow peaks and pines behind her.

dialogue.speaker: lal_ded
dialogue.text: I searched outside; the Beloved waited within.

i18n.hi: मैं बाहर ढूँढती रही; प्रिय भीतर बैठा इंतज़ार करता रहा.

panels.shot: wide interior of a Shaiva shrine, low light, priests in background while Lal Ded sits near the threshold
panels.action: Inside a dark stone shrine, priests tend a linga in the inner chamber while Lal Ded sits by the threshold, speaking softly to a small cluster of women and men who face her rather than the altar.

dialogue.text: Her verses carried Shaiva insight but questioned empty ritual, turning the sacred gaze from idol to consciousness itself.

i18n.hi: उसकी पंक्तियाँ शैव ज्ञान से भरी थीं, पर खोखले कर्मकांड पर प्रहार करतीं, नज़र को मूर्ति से हटाकर चेतना पर टिका देतीं.

panels.shot: street-level scene in a small Kashmiri town, with a wooden mosque roofline and a temple shikhara both visible, Lal Ded moving between
panels.action: A narrow town lane shows a wooden-roofed mosque on one side and a temple tower on the other as Lal Ded walks between them, greeted by both veiled women and Brahmin elders.

dialogue.text: Soon, her words slipped past the walls of sect and shrine; both Hindu and Muslim listeners claimed her as their own saint.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही उसके बोल मज़हबी दीवारें लाँघ गए; हिंदू–मुस्लिम दोनों ही उसे अपना संत मानने लगे.

panels.shot: medium shot with a young Nund Rishi in foreground listening intently to Lal Ded seated under a tree
panels.action: Under a chinar tree, Lal Ded sits cross-legged, speaking calmly, while a young ascetic figure, later known as Nund Rishi, listens with folded hands among other disciples.

dialogue.text: In time, Nund Rishi, founding voice of Kashmir’s Sufi Rishi order, would echo her, his verses honoring the depth of Lalla’s path.

i18n.hi: वक़्त के साथ, नुंद ऋषि, कश्मीर की सूफ़ी ऋषि परंपरा की पहली आवाज़, उसके सुर को दोहराएंगे, अपनी पंक्तियों से लल्ला की राह की गहराई को सलाम करेंगे.

panels.shot: dim palace hall interior, scribes at low desks writing by lamplight, a stern courtier overlooking them
panels.action: In a Sultanate court hall, robed scribes bend over palm-leaf manuscripts, ink and reed pens at work, while a court official surveys them with an air of importance.

dialogue.text: Yet the official histories of this age, written for sultans and ministers, do not speak her name; their ink followed power, not wandering mystics.

i18n.hi: पर इस दौर के सरकारी इतिहास, जो सुल्तानों और वज़ीरों के लिए लिखे गए, उसका नाम नहीं लेते; उनकी स्याही सत्ता के पीछे चली, भटकते फकीरों के पीछे नहीं.

panels.shot: contrast panel: scrolls locked in a chest on one side, and a village gathering around a storyteller on the other
panels.action: One half of the image shows tied manuscripts locked in a wooden chest; the other half shows villagers around a fire as an old storyteller raises a hand, his mouth open in mid-tale.

dialogue.text: Where chronicles are silent, oral memory speaks; it is in such fireside tales that we first find Lalla, centuries later set down by hagiographers.

i18n.hi: जहाँ तवारीख़ चुप हैं, वहीं ज़बानी याद बोलती है; आग के पास सुनाई जाने वाली इन्हीं दास्तानों में हम पहली बार लल्ला को पाते हैं, बाद में संत–कथाकार उन्हें लिखते हैं.

panels.shot: study table close-up in a later-century setting, with a hagiographic manuscript open, margin notes visible, candlelight
panels.action: A scholar’s hand from the sixteenth century hovers over an open Persian-script manuscript, the words of Tadhkirat-ul-Arifin flowing across the page in neat lines.

dialogue.text: Mulla Ali Raina’s Tadhkirat-ul-Arifin, written in 1587, gathers such tales, admiring yet embellishing, turning the elusive mystic into a saintly legend.

i18n.hi: मुल्ला अली रैना की ‘तज़किरत–उल–आरिफ़ीन’, १५८७ की किताब, ऐसे किस्से समेटती है – मुग्ध भी, सजावटी भी – धुँधली साधिका को एक पाक दास्तान बना देती है.

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of different Kashmiri landscapes—orchard, saffron field, mountain village—each with a figure reciting
panels.action: A sequence across the panel shows a herdsman in a high pasture, women in a saffron field, and a trader in a village bazaar, each mid-recitation, mouths shaped as if repeating the same vakh.

dialogue.text: Generations passed her verses from tongue to tongue; about one hundred and fifty vakhs survive, worn smooth by repetition, yet still edged with her questioning fire.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियाँ उसके वख ज़बान से ज़बान तक ले गईं; कोई डेढ़ सौ वख बचे हैं – दुहराव से घिसे, पर अब भी उसकी सवाल करती आग की धार लिए.

panels.shot: modern era study room, with Ranjit Hoskote’s book and other scholarly volumes on a table, window showing a faint outline of mountains
panels.action: In a contemporary study, books lie open on a desk—one titled with Lal Ded’s name—while outside the window the faint outline of snow mountains recalls the valley she walked.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars sift manuscripts and oral versions, comparing lines, weighing legend against language, careful not to fix Lalla into narrow, modern labels.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान पांडुलिपियाँ और ज़बानी रूप छाँटते हैं, पंक्तियाँ टटोलते हैं, क़िस्से को भाषा के तराज़ू पर तौलते हैं, सावधान कि लल्ला को तंग, नए ठप्पों में न जकड़ दें.

panels.shot: evocative medium shot of Lal Ded walking away down a misty path, back to the viewer, with villagers watching from doorways
panels.action: Lal Ded walks away along a misty village lane, her back turned, shawl trailing lightly; men and women stand in their doorways, watching her diminish into the fog.

dialogue.text: Her own life remains veiled: where she was born, whom she married, how she died—each tale differs, each listener fills the gaps anew.

i18n.hi: उसकी अपनी ज़िंदगी पर आज भी परदा है – कहाँ जन्मीं, किससे ब्याही, कैसे गईं – हर कहानी अलग, हर श्रोता अपने हिसाब से रिक्तियाँ भर देता है.

panels.shot: close-up of Lal Ded seated by a river rock, looking directly toward the viewer, expression calm and knowing
panels.action: Lal Ded sits on a smooth rock beside the river at dusk, hands resting loosely on her knees, as if she has paused mid-journey to look straight at the unseen listener.

dialogue.speaker: lal_ded
dialogue.text: Words will vanish; what you awaken to will not.

i18n.hi: शब्द मिट जाएँगे; जो तुम भीतर जागाओगे, वो नहीं.

panels.shot: final wide shot of the Kashmir valley at twilight, faint translucent image of Lal Ded’s figure overlaid with fields and rooftops
panels.action: As twilight falls over the Kashmir valley, roofs smoke and fields darken; a faint, translucent image of Lal Ded seems to hover above, her form dissolving into sky and mountain.

dialogue.text: Lal Ded gave Kashmiri speech a soul, proving that even when courts ignore a voice, a people can carry it, quietly, across centuries.

i18n.hi: लाल डेड ने कश्मीरी ज़ुबान को रूह दी, दिखा दिया कि दरबार चाहे आवाज़ दबा दे, कौम उसे चुपचाप, सदियों तक ढो सकती है.

title_i18n.en: Lal Ded Gives Kashmir a Voice
title_i18n.hi: लाल डेड ने कश्मीर को आवाज़ दी

subtitle_i18n.en: The Mystic Whose Song Outlived the Chronicles
subtitle_i18n.hi: वो सूफनिया जिस का गीत ज़मानों से लंबा चला
